land.text: the whole country, after the coup of 15 November 1889

capitals.name: Rio de Janeiro
capitals.note: The Brazil page does not name the earlier capital: Rio de Janeiro is the reading of 'the new capital city of Brasília, inaugurated in 1960' (the page has the royal court in Rio from 1807).

capitals.name: Brasília
capitals.note: Infobox capital; 'the new capital city of Brasília, inaugurated in 1960'.

correction.text: the whole country, the 1890 shape, from the coup of 15 November 1889

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1889: Cliopatria's Brazilian Republic row begins in 1890, but the Republic dates from 15 November 1889 (infobox 'Republic: 15 November 1889'; 'the monarchy was overthrown by a military coup'). The Empire of Brazil dossier ends in November 1889; the 1890 shape stands for the last weeks of 1889.

correction.text: the 1890 shape, valid for 1890-1902; Acre and the Roraima north-east are added from 1903-1904

keyframe_review.note: The shape stands for 1890-1902 only. It is 8.357 M km2 (infobox 8,510,346 km2; ratio 0.98) because it lacks Acre, held in Cliopatria by its Bolivia row, and the north-east of Roraima; Brazil occupied Acre in 1903 and the Treaty of Petrópolis of 17 November 1903 'gave Brazil the territory of Acre (191,000 km2)'. 1903 is carried by the ledger (occupation January, treaty in November) and 1904 by a new keyframe; Cliopatria switches only in 1905.

correction.text: Brazil with Acre, from the effective date of the Treaty of Petrópolis in March 1904

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1904: the treaty took effect on 10 March 1904 and Acre was incorporated 'by a presidential decree of April 7, 1904', but Cliopatria's shape with Acre begins in 1905. The 1905 shape (+159,833 km2, the page's 191,000 km2 for Acre; ratio 0.84, the page gives its figure without a citation) is used for 1904.

8.531 M km2 against the infobox 8,510,346 km2 (ratio 1.002). Of the 632 cells gained against 1890, 535 lie in the state of Acre, 19 in Amazonas, 15 in Peru and 7 in Bolivia (all held by Cliopatria's Bolivia row before) and 56 in the north-east of Roraima (held by no row); 6 cells are lost (3 to Bolivia, 3 to Britain). The Pirara page says the king ruled 'in favor of Britain' for 'the territory enclosed by the Tacutu and Ireng Rivers' and gives no areas, so the Roraima addition is an unverified reading.

Against 1905: 3 cells (759 km2) pass to Colombia near the Apaporis and 1 cell comes from Peru near Tabatinga. The Brazil-Colombia border page names the 1928 Tratado de Límites y Navegación Fluvial for the Apaporis-Amazon segment and the Vásquez Cobo-Martins treaty (no date on the page), and no areas: the shape stands, the cause is a reading.

Cliopatria's label for the Vargas years; the same 8.530 M km2 as 1928-1931. The Brazil page has 'the Constitutionalist Revolution in 1932, led by São Paulo's oligarchy' without territory, so no zone is cut. One state: the dossier brazilian-republic holds all four Cliopatria Names (Wikidata Q155).

unverified: page budget. Against 1932-1935: 6 cells (1,517 km2, around Porto Murtinho on the Paraguay frontier) are added, 4 from Cliopatria's Bolivia shape and 2 from Paraguay, and 1 cell goes to Paraguay. None of the five pages dates a Brazilian frontier change in the 1930s; the Brazil-Guyana page records only that boundary markers went up from 1932 to 1939.
Same shape as 1936-1944. 'Democracy was restored after Vargas' ousting in 1945'.
8.531 M km2, same as 1936-1945; the infobox gives 8,510,346 km2 (ratio 1.002). Brasília was inaugurated in 1960 but the frontier did not change.
Same shape as 1946-1962; the coup of April 1964 changed the regime, not the land.
Cliopatria's label for the military regime (1964-1985 on the page); same shape as 1946. Dossier brazilian-republic.
Same shape; the 1988 constitution 'defines it as a democratic federal republic' and made Amapá and Roraima states.
Unchanged. The infobox gives 8,510,346 km2 (body 8,515,767 km2); the shape is 8.531 M km2 (ratio 1.002).

region.text: the whole country at the proclamation

ledger.note: 15 November 1889: a military coup overthrows the monarchy and Brazil becomes a republic. 'the monarchy was overthrown by a military coup'; infobox 'Republic: 15 November 1889'. 'The early republican government was a military dictatorship'; civilians took power in 1894.

region.text: Acre, where the Republic of Acre had been proclaimed on 14 July 1899

ledger.note: 1903: Brazil occupies Acre. After a proclamation of 27 January 1903 Rio Branco's government 'ordered the Acre occupation and established a military government under the command of General Olimpio da Silveira'; the page dates the war 1899-1903 and a preliminary treaty on 21 March 1903.
17 November 1903: the occupation of Acre ends in annexation by the Treaty of Petrópolis, 'signed on November 17, 1903'.

region.text: the territory of Acre (191,000 km2), taken from Bolivia

ledger.note: 17 November 1903: Bolivia cedes Acre to Brazil. The treaty 'gave Brazil the territory of Acre (191,000 km2)' for two million pounds and a railway pledge (Acre War page: Bolivia yielded 'an approximate area of 191,000 square kilometers'); effective 10 March 1904, 'a presidential decree of April 7, 1904' incorporated Acre. Cliopatria draws the gain in 1905 and holds 576 of the 632 cells under its Bolivia row, including 15 cells of Peru's claim ('Brazil and Peru also claimed the territory'; the pages record no Peruvian cession).

region.text: Brazilian land between the Abuna and Madeira rivers

ledger.note: 17 November 1903: in exchange Brazil cedes 'over 3,000 km2 of Brazilian territory between the Abuna River and Madeira River' to Bolivia. [Region changed by reviewer am-08-h, 2026-10-19: a 60 km radius around -65.4,-10.0 drew about 11,300 km2; a 31 km radius around Abunã draws the page's 'over 3,000 km2' and matches Bolivia's mirror gain.]

region.text: the part of Roraima outside Cliopatria's 1890 shape, the Pirara region

ledger.note: 15 June 1904: the Pirara arbitration. The treaty to arbitrate was signed on 6 November 1901 and the King of Italy 'ruled in favor of Britain and granted them the territory enclosed by the Tacutu and Ireng Rivers'; the page gives no areas and does not say what Brazil received. Cliopatria's 1905 shape adds 56 cells of north-east Roraima held by no row: page silent, confidence 1.

region.text: the 3 cells on the Apaporis-Amazon segment

ledger.note: 1928: the Tratado de Límites y Navegación Fluvial. The Brazil-Colombia border page names it for 'the Apaporis-Amazon segment' and the Vásquez Cobo-Martins treaty (undated on the page); Cliopatria's 1928 shape passes 3 cells (759 km2) near the Apaporis to Colombia. The page gives no areas.
1928: Brazil gains 1 cell (253 km2) near Tabatinga from Cliopatria's Peru shape; no page dates or explains it.
October 1930: 'An armed revolution in 1930 ended the First Republic and brought Getúlio Vargas to power.' Civilians had held power 'until October 1930'. Same state and colour (rule 2).

1932: Cliopatria's label becomes 'Unitary State of Brazil' (1932-1945); the Brazil page does not use the name. The same year São Paulo's oligarchy rose in the Constitutionalist Revolution; the page gives no territory. Page silent: confidence 1.
1936: Cliopatria's shape adds 2 cells from its Paraguay shape (and 4 from Bolivia's) around Porto Murtinho; none of the pages opened dates a frontier change. Page silent: confidence 1.
1936: the other 4 of the 6 cells come from Cliopatria's Bolivia shape (the Chaco claim). Page silent: confidence 1.
1936: 1 cell (253 km2) passes to Paraguay in Cliopatria's shape. Page silent: confidence 1.
1937: 'The 1937 coup d'état resulted in the cancellation of the 1938 election and formalized Vargas as dictator, beginning the Estado Novo era.' Same state and colour.
1945: Vargas 'was swiftly overthrown in another military coup'; 'Democracy was restored after Vargas' ousting in 1945'. The Estado Novo ends; same state and colour.
1960: the capital moves to Brasília, 'the new capital city of Brasília, inaugurated in 1960' (the page does not name Rio de Janeiro as the old capital).
April 1964: the government 'was deposed in April 1964 by a coup that resulted in a military dictatorship' that 'ruled until 1985'. Cliopatria labels 1967-1986 'Federated Republic of Brazil'.
1967: Cliopatria's label becomes 'Federated Republic of Brazil'; the Brazil page does not mention a 1967 constitution. Page silent: confidence 1.
1985: 'Civilians returned to power in 1985 when José Sarney assumed the presidency.' Same state and colour.

5 October 1988: the current constitution is 'promulgated on 5 October 1988' and the last three territories become states ('Amapá and Roraima (which gained statehood)'). Cliopatria's 'Republic of Brazil' label starts in 1987.

wars.name: Acre War

zones.text: Acre: the Republic of Acre proclaimed on 14 July 1899, Plácido de Castro's rising on 6 August 1902, Brazilian occupation 1903

wars.outcome: Acrean victory: Bolivia surrendered Puerto Alonso on 24 January 1903; the Treaty of Petrópolis (17 November 1903) gave Brazil Acre (191,000 km2) for two million pounds, a railway pledge and over 3,000 km2 between the Abuna and Madeira.
wars.note: The page says the conflict 'had two phases between 1899 and 1903'; the Brazil page ends it in 1902. Peru's claim to the same land is on the page without outcome.

wars.name: Constitutionalist Revolution
wars.outcome: Rising of São Paulo's oligarchy against the Vargas government; the page gives no territory, dates or outcome.
wars.note: No zone is recorded: the page is silent on what the rebels held.

certainty.note: Amazon frontiers are unsettled: Acre is disputed with Bolivia and Peru until the Treaty of Petrópolis, and the Pirara region with British Guiana until the 1904 arbitration.

The Bolivian frontier is set by the Treaty of Petrópolis (1903), the Guyana frontier by the 1904 award modified in 1926 and marked 1932-1939, the Colombian frontier by the treaties of 1907 and 1928. The Peru, Paraguay, Uruguay, Argentina and Guianas frontiers are not covered by the pages opened and stay as Cliopatria draws them.

notes: Four Cliopatria rows share Wikidata Q155 and the same land: Brazilian Republic (1890-1931, 1946-1966), Unitary State of Brazil (1932-1945), Federated Republic of Brazil (1967-1986), Republic of Brazil (1987-2024). They are regimes of one republic (proclaimed 15 November 1889, the same land throughout, the shapes identical except for 1905, 1928 and 1936), so this is ONE dossier, listing all four Names and reviewing all 14 shapes (13 Cliopatria plus 1889 and 1904 new). The slugs unitary-state-of-brazil, federated-republic-of-brazil and republic-of-brazil (listed to other parts of am-08) should NOT get dossiers of their own; colours: one hue. Page budget 5 of 5. Not opened: the Misiones/Palmas question and the Amapá arbitration (Cliopatria's 1890 shape already includes Amapá), the Brazil-Peru treaty of 1909 and the Uruguay lagoon treaty of 1909, the Paraguay frontier (1936 cells), Fernando de Noronha and Trindade, the Constitutionalist Revolution's territory, the dates of the 1946 and 1967 constitutions, the Contestado War. Disagreements: Acre War page (1899-1903) against the Brazil page ('Acre War (1899–1902)'); the Treaty of Petrópolis infobox gives sealed 18 February 1904 and effective 10 March 1904 while the Acre War page gives 11 November 1903 as a ratification date; the Pirara award (15 June 1904 in the text; a citation dated 6 June 1904). The Roraima addition of 1905 is unexplained. Gazetteer names: all resolve (the Abuna-Madeira loss uses a coordinate radius at the Abuna confluence because 'Abuna' is not a gazetteer river). Counterparts: bolivia (am-08), republic-of-colombia (this part), republic-of-peru (am-08), paraguay (am-08), british-colonial-empire (eu-11, for the 1904 award).
